To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the susceptibility of individuals to reinfection with intestinal nematodes is related to the magnitude and type of the host cytokine response.

1) the cytokine response to parasite antigens in humans predicts future susceptibility to reinfection with intestinal nematodes; 2) the cytokine responses of individuals with a low response to parasite antigents are associated with a greater susceptibility to reinfection; and 3) the association between cytokine responses and reinfection is independent of the age of the host.

1) a T helper cell type-2 cytokine response to parasite antigens before treatment was associated with future susceptibility to gastrointestinal worms in a Camero- nian population, and 2) a weak T helper 2 response was a characteristic of persistently susceptible individuals.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the immunological basis of human susceptibility to gastrointestinal helminths.
the identification and characterization of the host factors associated with susceptibility to gastrointestinal nematology.
the development of novel approaches to the control of gastrointestinal nematode infection in humans.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a T helper cell type-2 response, in particular IL-13, is a key factor in susceptibility to reinfection with Ascaris and Trichuriasis in humans.
a weak T helper 2 response is a predictor of future susceptibility to gastrointestinal helminth infections.
a weak T helper type 2 response is associated with susceptibility to gastrointestinal nematology in humans.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
T helper cell type-2 responsiveness predicts future infection.
T helper cell type-2 responsiveness to helminth antigens, as measured by IL-5 and IL-13, is a useful predictor of future susceptibility to gastrointestinal helminths.
the ability of a human host to control infection with gastrointestinal nematodes is predicted by a T helper cell type-2 cytokine profile, which is established before the onset of infection.
The main takeaway from our work is that
host cytokine responses can predict susceptibility to reinfection, and that these responses are associated with age-dependent changes in worm burdens.
host cytokine responses are a promising biomarker of susceptibility to infection.
cytokine profiles may predict susceptibility to reinfection, which has implications for understanding the immunopathogenesis of helminth infections, and for the design of vaccines against helminths.
